'''Giorgio Kaniadakis''' ({{langx|el|Κανιαδάκης Γεώργιος}}; born on 5 June 1957 in [[Chania]]-[[Crete]], [[Greece]]) a Greek-Italian [[physicist]], is a Full Professor<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-14 |title=Giorgio Kaniadakis {{!}} Politecnico di Torino |url=https://www.polito.it/personale?p=giorgio.kaniadakis |access-date=2025-06-17 |website=www.polito.it |language=it}}</ref> of [[Theoretical physics|Theoretical Physics]] at [[Politecnico di Torino]], [[Italy]], and is credited with introducing the concept of [[Kaniadakis statistics|Kaniadakis entropy]]<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Hristopulos |first1=Dionissios T. |last2=da Silva |first2=Sérgio Luiz E. F. |last3=Scarfone |first3=Antonio M. |date=2025-02-27 |title=Twenty Years of Kaniadakis Entropy: Current Trends and Future Perspectives |journal=Entropy |language=en |volume=27 |issue=3 |pages=247 |doi=10.3390/e27030247 |doi-access=free |issn=1099-4300 |pmc=11941257 |pmid=40149171|bibcode=2025Entrp..27..247H }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Special Issue of Entropy, MPDI "Twenty Years of Kaniadakis Entropy: Current Trends and Future Perspectives" |url=https://www.mdpi.com/journal/entropy/special_issues/kaniadakis_entropy |access-date=2023-05-31 |website=www.mdpi.com |language=en}}</ref> and what is known as [[Kaniadakis statistics]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" /> Giorgio Kaniadakis is the founder and chairman of the ''[[SigmaPhi International Conference on Statistical Physics|SigmaPhi]]''  ''[[SigmaPhi International Conference on Statistical Physics|International Conference on Statistical Physics]]'', which is organized every three years in collaboration with the [[European Physical Society]].[http://www.sigmaphi.polito.it/]

== Education ==
In 1975 Giorgio Kaniadakis moved to Italy where he obtained the [[Bachelor's degree|Bachelor's]] and [[Master's degree]]s in [[Nuclear engineering|Nuclear Engineering]] in 1981 from [[Politecnico di Torino]]. In 1985, he obtained a [[Master's degree]] in [[Nuclear physics|Nuclear Physics]] from [[University of Turin|Università di Torino]] ([[Italy]]) and in 1989 he received a [[Ph.D. degree]] in [[Physics]] from [[Polytechnic University of Turin|Politecnico di Torino]] with grant of the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|International Center for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)]] of [[Trieste]], [[Italy]].

== Career ==
Since 1991 Kaniadakis is a permanent [[Faculty (division)|faculty]] member at Department of Physics (now Department of Applied Science and Technology) of the [[Politecnico di Torino]] as Researcher, Senior Researcher (1994), Aggregate Professor (2010), Associate Professor (2014), and Full Professor (2019).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Politecnico di Torino |url=https://www.polito.it/node/137 |access-date=2023-05-31 |website=www.polito.it |language=it}}</ref>

== Research ==
[[Kaniadakis statistics]]<ref name=":2" /> (known also as κ-statistics) is a theory based on [[Kaniadakis statistics|Kaniadakis entropy]]<ref name=":2" /> (known also as κ-entropy) that was introduced in the trilogy of papers published between 2001 and 2005.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=G. |date=2001-07-15 |title=Non-linear kinetics underlying generalized statistics |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378437101001844 |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and Its Applications |language=en |volume=296 |issue=3 |pages=405–425 |doi=10.1016/S0378-4371(01)00184-4 |arxiv=cond-mat/0103467 |bibcode=2001PhyA..296..405K |s2cid=44275064 |issn=0378-4371}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=G. |date=2002-11-25 |title=Statistical mechanics in the context of special relativity |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevE.66.056125 |journal=Physical Review E |language=en |volume=66 |issue=5 |article-number=056125 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.66.056125 |pmid=12513574 |arxiv=cond-mat/0210467 |bibcode=2002PhRvE..66e6125K |s2cid=45635888 |issn=1063-651X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=G. |date=2005-09-09 |title=Statistical mechanics in the context of special relativity. II. |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevE.72.036108 |journal=Physical Review E |language=en |volume=72 |issue=3 |article-number=036108 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.72.036108 |pmid=16241516 |arxiv=cond-mat/0507311 |bibcode=2005PhRvE..72c6108K |s2cid=18115408 |issn=1539-3755}}</ref> [[Kaniadakis statistics]] can be traced back to the first principles of [[Special relativity|Special Relativity]].<ref name=":1" /> It answers the open problem on how the temperature of a body is transformed in a moving inertial frame by selecting the [[Planck-Einstein Relation|Planck-Einstein transformation law]]. Within [[Kaniadakis statistics|κ-statistics]], Kaniadakis entropy emerges as the relativistic generalization of [[Boltzmann's entropy formula|Boltzmann's entropy]] exactly as happens with relativistic energy which turns out to be the relativistic generalization of energy of [[classical physics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bíró |first=Tamás S. |date=2009 |title=Statistical Power Law Tails in High-Energy Phenomena |journal=The European Physical Journal A |language=en |volume=40 |issue=3 |article-number=255 |bibcode=2009EPJA...40..255B |doi=10.1140/epja/i2009-10791-8 |issn=1434-6001 |s2cid=123489626 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Kaniadakis' theoretical framework, alongside the proposed statistical theory, also provides a mathematical formalism (also known as [[Kaniadakis statistics|κ-mathematics]]) which is isomorphic to ordinary mathematics.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=Giorgio |date=2024-05-07 |title=Relativistic Roots of κ-Entropy |journal=Entropy |language=en |volume=26 |issue=5 |pages=406 |doi=10.3390/e26050406 |pmid=38785655 |doi-access=free |arxiv=2405.07678 |bibcode=2024Entrp..26..406K |issn=1099-4300}}</ref>

[[Cosmic ray]]s are a relativistic particle system composed of normal nuclei as in the standard cosmic abundances of matter, and approximately can be viewed as an equivalent statistical system of identical [[relativistic particle]]s with masses near the mass of the [[proton]]. For a long time, it has been known that the cosmic ray spectrum is not exponential, and then it violates the [[Boltzmann statistics]]. The presence in the cosmic ray spectrum of power-law tails, which extends over 13 decades in energy and spans 33 decades in particle flux, represents an important experimental test of the correctness and predictability of [[Kaniadakis statistics]].<ref name=":2" />

The statistical theory rooted on [[Kaniadakis statistics|Kaniadakis entropy]] has significantly influenced scientific literature, both in establishing its theoretical foundations and in numerous application areas.
